title: Read-decide-write across processes
note: Every mutation here restores a defect that four to six real processes found and that no single-threaded test could see. The writer lock makes one APPEND atomic; it never made read-decide-write atomic, and every reducer in this package does exactly that. X1-X3 attack the decision happening under the lock and against a re-read projection -- remove any of them and two processes each move the same job out of the same state, leaving a perfect hash chain nobody can replay. X4 attacks the dry run, which is what stops a writer producing a record its own reducer will reject. X5 attacks the order in which verify() samples the witness against the log: sampled in the same order as the write, another process's ordinary append reads as TRUNCATED. X6 attacks the retry budget, which was consulted only where a worker REPORTED a failure -- so a worker that simply died requeued the job forever. X7 attacks reconcile's tolerance of a world that moved under its scan.

mutations.name: X1_the_decision_happens_outside_the_lock
mutations.find:
with self.exclusive():
            report = self._checked_head()
            kwargs = decide(report.head_seq)
mutations.replace:
report = self._checked_head()
        kwargs = decide(report.head_seq)
        with self.exclusive():
            report = self._checked_head()
mutations.rationale: the decision is made before the lock is taken, so two processes decide against the same state and both write; the chain stays perfect and the log stops being replayable

mutations.name: X2_the_projection_is_not_re_read_before_deciding
mutations.rationale: the lock is held and the decision is still made against a projection loaded before another process wrote -- exclusion without a re-read protects nothing

mutations.name: X3_the_store_decides_from_a_stale_projection
mutations.rationale: two verifiers each take the same record under review, and the second record moves it from a state the replay has already left

mutations.name: X4_a_record_the_reducer_will_reject_is_written_anyway
mutations.rationale: check_edge asks whether the state machine permits the edge; the reducer asks more -- whether a requeue is reclaiming a lease that is still live -- and a record that satisfies the first and not the second is durable and unreplayable

mutations.name: X5_the_witness_is_sampled_after_the_log
mutations.rationale: the witness is sampled HERE, after the log has been read, which is the order the writer uses -- so another process's ordinary append lands between the two samples and reads as TRUNCATED, damage, for a log that was merely being written

mutations.name: X6_a_lapsed_lease_does_not_spend_the_retry_budget
mutations.find:
if job.attempts >= job.max_attempts:
                # THE RETRY BUDGET HAS TO COUNT LAPSES TOO.
mutations.replace:
if False:
                # THE RETRY BUDGET HAS TO COUNT LAPSES TOO.
mutations.rationale: a worker that dies reports nothing, so the budget is never consulted and the job is handed to a new worker forever -- the budget bounded nothing in the failure mode it exists for

mutations.name: X7_reconcile_cannot_survive_the_world_moving_under_it
mutations.rationale: reconcile scans and then writes; another process dispatching in between makes the whole convergence pass raise instead of skipping one job and continuing

mutations.name: X8_two_processes_may_create_the_same_record_id
mutations.rationale: a record id is a claim to a name; two creates make one of the two proposers the recorded author of a record they did not write, and the replay refuses the second
